header.title: Confidential recruiter pitch: Head of Platform role (via Brightline Talent)

evidence: On 1 October 2026 the user took a call from Dana Whitlock, a recruiter at Brightline Talent, about a Head of Platform role
The opportunity offered a base salary of €145,000–€165,000, a 15% annual bonus target
The user agreed to a follow-up call on 8 October 2026
pieces.body: On 1 October 2026 I took a call from Dana Whitlock, a recruiter at Brightline Talent, about a Head of Platform role at an unnamed client: a Series C payments company headquartered in Lisbon with about 400 employees. I was asked to keep the details confidential until the client agrees to disclose its name. The Head of Platform role would lead three platform teams (about 22 engineers) covering infrastructure, developer tooling and internal APIs, reporting to the CTO. It offered a base salary of €145,000–€165,000, a 15% annual bonus target and equity Dana called "meaningful" without a number. It was fully remote within Portugal (Lisbon office optional), with a January 2027 start. The hiring process would have four stages: CTO call, system design session, leadership panel, reference check. I told Dana I was interested, but that I had not managed more than one team before and wanted the equity terms in writing before going further. Dana would send a one-page summary by email, and we agreed a follow-up call on 8 October 2026 after Dana confirms whether the client will reveal its name.

pieces.body: On 4 August 2026 I heard that Quillstone, a London-based e-commerce infrastructure company, did not select me for the Engineering Manager position on the Payments Reliability team. I had applied in early July 2026 after seeing the role on LinkedIn and reached the final round on 30 July 2026, a two-hour panel with Director of Engineering Priyanka Raman and two engineering managers. Priyanka Raman's rejection email said the panel was impressed by my incident-response examples but chose a candidate with more experience running performance reviews and hiring loops. I accepted her offer of a 20-minute feedback call on Monday 10 August 2026. Quillstone recruiter Owen Pike was slow to reply throughout, often taking a week. I felt disappointed but relieved, since the role required three days a week in the London office, and I decided to send a short thank-you note.

pieces.body: In September 2026 I was in the hiring process for the Senior Firmware Engineer position at Halvorsen Robotics, a warehouse-automation company in Trondheim, which I found through a referral from Ingrid Sæther. Screening call on 2 September 2026 with recruiter Tomas Berg: the Halvorsen Robotics role is fully remote within European time zones with one on-site week in Trondheim per quarter, and the salary band is NOK 950,000–1,150,000 a year plus an annual bonus of up to 10%. Technical interview on 9 September 2026 with Ingrid Sæther and senior engineer Aksel Moe covered embedded Rust, real-time scheduling on ARM Cortex-M and a CAN bus trace debugging exercise; I felt weakest on IEC 61508 safety certification. Final round on 16 September 2026 with VP of Engineering Lene Haugland (firmware group of 14 engineers across three teams); Halvorsen Robotics expected a decision by end of September 2026. I told Lene my earliest start date would be 2 November 2026.
pieces.title: Halvorsen Robotics Senior Firmware Engineer hiring process (Sep 2026)

pieces.body: As of June 2026 I'm building Tern, a personal budgeting app for iPhone and Mac, as a side project with my friend Sofia Antunes, who handles the design. I started Tern in January 2026 and aimed for a public TestFlight beta by the end of September 2026. Tern imports bank exports as CSV and OFX files rather than connecting to banks directly, because I don't want to store bank credentials or pay for an aggregator such as Plaid. Tern will be free with a one-time €9.99 unlock for multiple accounts and no subscription. Sofia wants a dark, high-contrast look, I prefer following the system appearance, and we agreed Tern will support both. I spend Sunday mornings on Tern, about four hours a week. The Tern repository is private on GitHub under Sofia's account for now.
pieces.title: Tern budgeting app side project with Sofia Antunes

pieces.body: My partner Rui and I spent two weeks in Japan from 11 to 25 April 2026: five nights in Tokyo, six in Kyoto and three in Osaka. It was our first trip to Asia. We flew TAP from Lisbon to Tokyo via Frankfurt; the Frankfurt connection was tight and our luggage arrived a day late. In Kyoto we stayed at the Hanaori ryokan near Gion, the highlight of the trip. My favourite meal was at Tenkuu, a tempura counter in Osaka. Finding vegetarian food for Rui in Osaka was harder than expected; shojin ryori temple restaurants in Kyoto were easiest. I got a Suica card at the airport and topped it up twice. Rui twisted an ankle on the Fushimi Inari trail on 19 April 2026 and was fine after a few days. The Japan trip cost about €6,200 for both of us, slightly over our €5,500 budget.
pieces.title: Japan trip with Rui, 11–25 April 2026

pieces.body: I signed a freelance contract with Oakhurst Media, a Dublin podcast network, on 26 March 2026 to rebuild the iOS client of its listener app, running 6 April to 30 September 2026. Day rate €720 (Oakhurst first offered €650), four days a week with Fridays free for other clients. Payment 30 days from invoice, invoiced monthly (I asked for 15 and accepted 30 for the higher rate). It includes an NDA forbidding naming Oakhurst's unreleased features publicly; I may list Oakhurst as a client in my portfolio. IP transfers to Oakhurst on payment; either side can end it with 14 days' notice. An electronic signature was fine.

pieces.body: I injured my right knee on 14 March 2026 playing five-a-side football (twisted on landing, felt a pop, swelling that evening). My GP Dr. Helena Costa (USF Alvalade) saw me two days later and referred me for an MRI. The MRI on 2 April 2026 at Clínica Lumiar showed a grade 2 medial meniscus tear with no ligament damage. Orthopaedic surgeon Dr. Paulo Mendes advised against surgery for now and prescribed eight weeks of physiotherapy; cycling and swimming were fine, but no football or running on hard surfaces until cleared. At the 20 July 2026 review he said the knee was healing well, cleared gentle jogging on grass or treadmill from August 2026, said football should wait until at least October 2026, and recommended home exercises three times a week for another three months.
pieces.title: Right knee meniscus tear 2026: diagnosis and recovery

pieces.body: For my 2026 knee meniscus tear, physiotherapy started on 8 April 2026 with Joana Reis at Fisio Campo de Ourique, Tuesdays and Fridays at 8:00, focusing on quadriceps and hip strengthening, balance and gradual load. I find single-leg balance exercises hardest and tend to skip them at home, which Joana flagged. By mid-June 2026 I could walk an hour pain-free and climb stairs normally, but kneeling was still uncomfortable.

The feedback forms gave the talk 4.6 out of 5; several people said the live demo was the best part, and two said the CRDT section was too fast.

pieces.body: On 24 September 2026 I gave the talk "Offline-first sync without tears" at NordicSwift 2026 in Oslo. It was 30 minutes plus Q&A, about conflict resolution with CRDTs in a SwiftData app, with Tern as the example, and about 250 people attended. I was nervous beforehand and rehearsed five times with my partner, which helped a lot. The NordicSwift organisers covered my flight and two hotel nights, and I paid for an extra night to see Oslo. I had to ask them for a USB-C to HDMI adapter. The feedback forms rated the talk 4.6 out of 5: several people said the live demo was the best part, and two said the CRDT section was too fast. The slides are on Speaker Deck, and the recording was expected on YouTube in October 2026.
pieces.title: NordicSwift 2026 talk in Oslo: "Offline-first sync without tears"

evidence: It was their first conference talk in English; before, they had only spoken at local meetups in Lisbon.

header.title: Interview loop at Verdant Grid (Staff Data Engineer)

evidence: The user completed the interview loop for the Staff Data Engineer role last week.
The user was weaker in the live SQL exercise and ran out of time on the last window-function question.
They expect to hear back by Friday next week.
pieces.body: I completed the interview loop for the Staff Data Engineer role at Verdant Grid in the week of 5 October 2026: four interviews, on Tuesday 6 and Thursday 8 October 2026. Verdant Grid builds forecasting software for electricity grids and has about 120 employees, mostly in Copenhagen. In the system design interview, Mette had me design a pipeline for smart-meter readings and praised my enthusiasm and my questions about data quality. The hiring manager, Jonas, said the role is fully remote with a yearly team week in Copenhagen, and the team uses Python and dbt on Snowflake. I was weaker in the live SQL exercise and ran out of time on the last window-function question. The salary range given was DKK 85,000–95,000 a month. I sent my resume as a PDF to the recruiter the same day. As of 14 October 2026 I expected to hear back by Friday 23 October 2026. I like that Verdant Grid's product is about the energy transition but am unsure about the pay; if an offer comes I would negotiate for DKK 100,000 a month.
pieces.title: Verdant Grid Staff Data Engineer interview loop (October 2026)

header.title: Recruiter call about a CTO role

evidence: Yesterday the user had a call with Marta Sousa, an independent recruiter, about a CTO position at Lumen Health
The role pays €110,000 a year plus 1.5% equity vesting over four years, with a one-year cliff.
told Marta they would reply by the end of next week
pieces.body: On 1 September 2026 I had a call with independent recruiter Marta Sousa about a CTO position at Lumen Health, a 35-person Porto startup making appointment software for dental clinics. The Lumen Health CTO role pays €110,000 a year plus 1.5% equity vesting over four years with a one-year cliff; I said the equity sounded low and Marta thought 2% might be possible. It is hybrid, two days a week in the Porto office (the earlier fully-remote job ad is out of date), meaning commuting by train from Lisbon or moving. The founders want the CTO to still code in the first year, grow the team from 6 to 15 engineers, and start an iOS app; the stack is Kotlin backend and React web. Lumen Health raised a €6M seed in March 2026 and has about 20 months of runway. The process would be a conversation with the two founders, a half-day with the team and a reference call. I'm interested in the iOS work and being a CTO but worried about the commute and runway, and I saw the founders' past work together at a hospital software company as a good sign. I wanted to discuss it with my partner and told Marta I'd reply by the end of the following week (around 11 September 2026).
pieces.title: Lumen Health CTO role recruiter call with Marta Sousa (Sept 2026)

pieces.body: As of 2 September 2026 I was considering a CTO role that recruiter Marta told me about. Marta said the founders wanted an answer before the end of September 2026 so the new CTO could start in January 2027. The CTO role comes with a €3,000 yearly training budget, which I would spend on conferences. The office is near São Bento station, about ten minutes' walk from the platform, so commuting by train from Lisbon would take about three hours each way door to door. I planned to look up the founders on LinkedIn before replying.
